hindi: इन छह के दो-दो के संयोग से तीस भेद होते हैं।
english: Of these six, from the combination of two, there are thirty varieties.
notes: The six are not named in this unit. Thirty is as printed; the text does not explain how the count is reached (it is not the number of pairs of six). 'triṃśadbhedā bhavanti' is regular sandhi (āḥ before b becomes ā).

hindi: अकेलों के साथ छत्तीस को जाने, उपद्रवों सहित भी।
english: Together with the single (ones), one should know thirty-six, also with their complications (upadrava).
notes: The noun for the thirty-six is not stated; no noun is added. Thirty-six equals the thirty of 124 plus six, but the text does not say so. 'kevalaiḥ' read as 'single, alone'; 'sa-upadravān' is accusative plural, agreeing with the unstated object of vidyāt. GROUPING: 125 follows on 124 and 126-127 name the upadravas.

words.gloss: colic pain; pravāhikā (straining at stool, tenesmus; standard); distension; cutting pain; loss of appetite; fevers

hindi: शूल, प्रवाहिका यानी मल के लिए ज़ोर लगना, आध्मान, परिकर्ती, अरुचि यानी भोजन की अनिच्छा और ज्वर यानी बुखार।
english: Colic pain (śūla), pravāhikā (straining at stool, tenesmus), distension (ādhmāna), cutting pain (parikarti), loss of appetite (aruci) and fevers (jvara).
notes: GROUPING: 126 and 127 form one statement; the verb vidyāt and the governing phrase 'upadravān' are in 127, so this unit is a bare list (no verb supplied). The final member is accusative plural (jvarān), the rest are compound members. Printed 'parikartyaruci' = parikarti + aruci (sandhi i+a = ya). 'parikarti' read as cutting pain (cf. parikartikā); standard.

words.gloss: thirst; bewilderment; burning; fainting; and so on

hindi: तृष्णा यानी प्यास, मोह यानी भ्रम, दाह यानी जलन, मूर्च्छा यानी बेहोशी आदि को भी इनके उपद्रव जाने।
english: Thirst (tṛṣ), bewilderment (moha), burning (dāha), fainting (mūrcchā) and so on one should know as the complications (upadrava) of these.
notes: GROUPING: completes 126 (the list there and this list are the objects of vidyāt). 'tṛṇmoha' = tṛṣ + moha (ṣ-final becomes ṇ before m). 'eṣām' is not specified further in the unit (it refers to the varieties of 124-125).

hindi: वहाँ आम में, अस्पष्ट शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ पर, पान, कटु, अम्ल और लवण से युक्त,
english: There, in āma (undigested matter), the drink — on a conjectural reading of the unclear word 'tara' — joined with pungent, sour and salty (ones),

text_flags.why: possible: 'tarapāna' with avagraha is not a known word; 'antarapāna' is one guess (metre is unaffected); same form in 135

notes: GROUPING: 128 and 129 form one statement; the predicate 'pācanam śasyate' is in 129. The printed 'tarapānam' (after an avagraha) is unclear: no reading is built on it. Possible 'antara-pāna' (a drink taken between things) or 'itara-pāna', but neither is certain and neither is applied; the same word recurs in 135. Sandhi is regular otherwise.

hindi: पाचन प्रशस्त है; आम में तो बस्ति का निषेध किया जाता है।
english: A digestive (pācana) is recommended; in āma, basti (enema) is indeed forbidden.
notes: GROUPING: continues 128. The grammar of 'pācanam' (neuter singular) with the drink of 128 is a natural reading but the link is not certain.

words.gloss: wind-destroying; binding (grāhin); belonging to the group

hindi: मल में वातनाशक और ग्राही वर्ग की बस्ति प्रशस्त है।
english: A basti (enema) of the group of wind-destroying and binding (grāhin) (ones) is recommended in stool.
notes: 'grāhin' = binding, checking the bowels; kept as grāhi. 'vargīya' = belonging to the group (varga); the members of the group are not listed. 'in stool' is literal (śakṛti); what condition is meant is not stated.

hindi: वायु में मधुर और अम्ल, स्पष्ट लवण वाली स्नेहबस्ति।
english: An oil enema (sneha-basti), sweet and sour, with the salt evident, in wind (samīraṇa).
notes: Elliptical: no verb; 'is recommended' of 130 is carried over, none supplied. 'samīraṇa' (wind) is read as vāta; kept as 'wind'.

hindi: रक्त में, रक्त से, पित्त और रक्त में कसैला, मधुर और तिक्त।
english: In blood, with blood, in pitta-and-blood (pittāsra): astringent, sweet and bitter.
notes: Elliptical: the noun 'basti' is not in the line (carried from the series, none supplied). 'rakte raktena' is odd (locative then instrumental of the same word); the sense of the pair is not clear and no reading is built on it. 'pitta-asra' read as pitta-and-blood. Tastes: kaṣāya = astringent; the -ka ending is the usual adjectival suffix.

words.gram: caus. pass. pres. part., m. loc. sg. √sṛ

hindi: कफ के सरकाए जाते समय बस्ति कसैली, कटु और तिक्त हो।
english: When Kapha is being made to move (sāryamāṇa), the basti is astringent, pungent and bitter.
notes: 'sāryamāṇe' read as the passive-causative present participle of √sṛ (being made to move or flow); this is the plain reading but not secure. No verb in the Sanskrit; 'is' supplied only as the copula of a locative absolute statement. Kaṣāya is the taste here (astringent), not a decoction.

hindi: मल से, अथवा वायु से, अथवा आम से; मल में, अथवा वायुओं से।
english: With stool, or with wind, or with āma; in stool, or else with winds.

text_flags.why: possible (very likely): the nukta-k stands for kṛ; same print habit in 143 'śaqacchoṇitayoḥ'
possible: final visarga dropped (the instrumental plural anilaiḥ is expected; metre needs 16 syllables as printed)

notes: GROUPING: 134 and 135 form one statement (the predicate is in 135: saṃsṛṣṭe ... syāt). The line is a list of combinations (saṃsarga) and is odd: stool appears twice (śakṛt, varcas) and the cases vary (instrumental, locative); no reading is built on the sense. Print: 'śaqatā' (q is a nukta sign) for śakṛtā; final visarga of 'anilai' lost.

hindi: संसृष्ट में, अस्पष्ट शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ पर, पान कटु, अम्ल और लवण से युक्त हो।
english: In the mixed (case), there should be the drink — on a conjectural reading of the unclear word 'tara' — joined with pungent, sour and salty (ones).
notes: GROUPING: completes 134. The word printed 'tarapānam' is unclear, as in 128 (see there); no reading is built on it. 'saṃsṛṣṭe' (mixed, combined) has no noun in the unit.

hindi: पित्त से, आम में, रक्त से, उसी प्रकार; अथवा फिर उन दोनों का आम से।
english: With pitta, in āma, with blood, likewise; or again, of those two, with āma.
notes: GROUPING: 136 and 137 form one statement (predicate 'bhavet pānam' in 137). A list of combinations; the sense of 'tayoḥ āmena' (of/in the two, with āma) is not fully clear, so the literal order is kept; 'tayoḥ' could be genitive or locative dual.

words.gloss: of the two that are mixed

hindi: दो संसृष्टों में कटु, मधुर और तिक्त सहित पान हो।
english: Of the two that are mixed, there should be a drink with pungent, sweet and bitter (tastes).
notes: GROUPING: completes 136. 'saṃsṛṣṭayoḥ' (genitive or locative dual) has no noun in the unit; 'sa-kaṭuka' is read as 'with pungent' (kaṭuka = kaṭu).

hindi: उसी प्रकार कफ से संसृष्ट आम में कसैला, कटु और तिक्त।
english: Likewise, in āma mixed with Kapha, (one) astringent, pungent and bitter.
notes: Elliptical: 'pānam' (drink) of 137 is carried over (neuter ending), none supplied. Printed token "''me" = āme (double avagraha stands for ā). Kaṣāya here is the taste (astringent).

hindi: आम से तो कफ के युक्त होने पर कसैला, लव शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ पर, औषध।
english: But when Kapha is joined with āma: a medicine (auṣadha), astringent and — on a conjectural reading of the doubtful word 'lava' —

text_flags.why: possible: the line is 15 syllables as printed and 16 with lavaṇa (ṇa dropped); not certain

notes: The compound 'kaṣāyalavauṣadham' is doubtful at 'lava': it may be a truncated lavaṇa (salt), which would give a 16-syllable line, but this is not certain and no reading is built on it. The English breaks off because the sense of the damaged word is not secure. kaṣāya = astringent taste or decoction: not fixed here.

hindi: वात से, मल में अथवा पित्त में; मल, पित्त और रक्त में, उसी प्रकार वायु में,
english: With wind, in stool or in pitta; in stool, pitta and blood, likewise in wind,

text_flags.why: possible: ś for ṣ; viṣ (viṭ) = excrement, locative viṣi; same form in 145

notes: GROUPING: 140 and 141 form one statement (predicate 'syāt ... bastiḥ uttamaḥ' in 141). Print 'viśi' read as viṣi (locative of viṣ/viṭ, excrement); the same print form recurs in 145. Pure list of combinations.

hindi: संसृष्ट में कसैली, खट्टी और मधुर बस्ति उत्तम होगी।
english: In the mixed (case), a basti astringent, sour and sweet would be best.
notes: GROUPING: completes 140. 'syāt' with 'uttamaḥ' is read as 'would be best'.

hindi: वात से और रक्त में बस्ति मधुर, अम्ल और तिक्त करनी चाहिए।
english: With wind and in blood, the basti should be done sweet, sour and bitter.
notes: Literal: 'kāryaḥ' (should be done, made). 'with wind' and 'in blood' are the conditions as printed.

hindi: मल और रक्त के, पित्त और मल के, रक्त और पित्त के,
english: Of stool and blood, of pitta and stool, of blood and pitta,

text_flags.why: possible (very likely): the nukta-k stands for kṛ, as in 134

notes: GROUPING: 143 and 144 form one statement (predicate in 144: basti ... in mutual combination). Genitive or locative dual throughout, so 'of' is chosen; 'in' is also possible. Print 'śaqacchoṇitayoḥ' read as śakṛc-śoṇitayoḥ (sandhi śakṛt + ś = śakṛc-ch).

hindi: परस्पर संयोग में बस्ति कसैली, मधुर और तिक्त हो।
english: In mutual combination, the basti is astringent, sweet and bitter.
notes: GROUPING: completes 143. No verb in the Sanskrit; 'is' is the copula of the statement. 'anyonya' = one another (mutual).

hindi: कफ से, मल में अथवा पित्त में; कफ में मल, पित्त और रक्त के साथ,
english: With Kapha, in stool or in pitta; in Kapha, with stool, pitta and blood,

text_flags.why: possible: same print form and reading as in 140

notes: GROUPING: 145 and 146 form one statement (predicate in 146). 'viśi' is read as viṣi (see 140); flagged again for this occurrence.

hindi: संसृष्ट में कटु, तिक्त और कसैली बस्ति उत्तम होगी।
english: In the mixed (case), a basti pungent, bitter and astringent would be best.

text_flags.why: probable: 'kadu' is not a word; kaṭu fits the sense and the series of tastes in 133, 138

notes: GROUPING: completes 145. Print 'kadutikta...' read as kaṭutikta (the Devanagari has da for ṭa).

hindi: वायु से संसृष्ट कफ में कटु, तिक्त और अम्ल बस्ति हो।
english: In Kapha mixed with wind, there should be a basti pungent, bitter and sour.
notes: 'saṃsṛṣṭe' agrees with 'kaphe', with 'vāyunā' as the thing it is mixed with.

hindi: रक्त में, जो कफ से मिला हो, मधुर, कटु और तिक्त।
english: But in blood mingled with Kapha: sweet, uṣaṇa (pungent) and bitter.
notes: Elliptical: 'basti' of the series is carried over, none supplied. 'uṣaṇa' is read as the pungent taste (also pepper); if it is a misprint for uṣṇa the sense would be 'hot'. Not applied.

hindi: कफ से संसृष्ट वायु में कटु, अम्ल और लवण हो।
english: In wind mixed with Kapha, it should be pungent, sour and salty.
notes: The subject (basti) is not stated; 'it' is used. Compare 147, where Kapha is mixed with wind.

words.gloss: three; four; five; six; by combining

hindi: तीन, चार, पाँच और छह के योग से इसी प्रकार विकल्प करे।
english: By combining three, four, five or six, one should vary (it) in just this way.

text_flags.why: possible: 'āvem' is not a word; yogena + evam + eva gives 16 syllables and a sense

notes: Printed 'yogenāvemeva' is read as yogena + evam + eva (naivameva garbled in the scan). The object of vikalpayet and the things combined are not stated.

hindi: और यह युक्ति, जो अतिसार यानी दस्त के लिए कही गई है, सब रोगों में भी मानी गई है।
english: And this method (yukti), stated for atisāra (diarrhoea), is held also in all diseases.
notes: Atisāra = diarrhoea (standard). 'atisāroktā' = atisāra-uktā, 'stated for/in atisāra'. 'smṛtā' = remembered, held (traditionally taught).

hindi: एक साथ, अस्पष्ट शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ पर, छह के संयोग में पाचन हो।
english: At once, on a conjectural reading of the unclear word 'sadrusam', in the combination of six, there should be a pācana (digestive).

text_flags.why: possible: 'sadrusam' is not a word; ṣaḍ-rasam fits 153, metre is 16 either way

notes: 'sadrusam' is not a known word and is left unsplit and unread. It may be ṣaḍ-rasam (six tastes), as in 153 ṣaḍrasika, but that is only a guess and is not applied. Sense of the unit therefore uncertain.

hindi: आम से रहित पाँचों के लिए छह रसों वाली बस्ति हितकर है।
english: But of the five (ones) free of āma, a basti having six tastes is beneficial.

text_flags.why: probable: stray r; nirāmāṇām (of those free of āma) is regular and keeps 16 syllables

notes: Printed 'nirāmārṇām' has a stray r; nirāmāṇām is the regular genitive plural (ṇ after r is not blocked by m). The five are not named. 'ṣaḍrasika' = having six rasas (tastes).

words.gloss: udumbara (cluster fig, Ficus racemosa; standard); unripe fruits
jambū (jamun, Syzygium cumini; probable, reading uncertain); mango (Mangifera indica; standard); udumbara; barks

hindi: उदुम्बर यानी गूलर के कच्चे फल, जामुन, आम और गूलर की छालें।
english: Unripe fruits (śalāṭu) of udumbara (cluster fig), the barks of jambū (probably jamun), āmra (mango) and udumbara.

text_flags.why: possible: jambu + āmra gives jaṃbvām; the printed 'byā' may be a misprint; metre is unchanged

notes: GROUPING: 154 and 155 are one list; 156 gives the preparation (piṣṭvā ... pacet). Printed 'jaṃbyāmra' (jambī/jambya + āmra) is read as jambū or jambu + āmra; possibly a misprint for jaṃbvāmra. 'śalāṭu' = unripe fruit (standard). The bark list is read as the barks of the three trees. Hindi names: गूलर, जामुन, आम.

words.gloss: sarja (sal tree, Shorea robusta); resin (sarjarasa; standard)

hindi: शंख, सर्जरस यानी साल का राल, लाख और कत्तृण, और एक पल के अंश वाला।
english: Conch shell (śaṅkha), sarjarasa (resin of the sal tree), lac (lākṣā) and kattṛṇa (a grass, unidentified), and with a pala as the portion.
notes: GROUPING: continues 154. 'palāṃśikam' is singular; whether it applies to all items (each one pala) is not stated, so the literal 'with a pala as the portion' is kept. Pala is a unit of weight. kattṛṇa unidentified here (earlier chunk: a grass, identity uncertain).

hindi: पीसकर उनके साथ एक प्रस्थ घी को, दूध से दुगुना किया हुआ, पकाए।
english: Having ground (them), one should cook with these a prastha (a measure) of ghee, doubled with milk.
notes: Completes 154-155. 'kṣīradviguṇitam' = made twofold by milk (the amount of milk is thus twice the ghee on one reading); the text does not state the ratio, so the literal wording is kept. The grammar of the 'doubled' word (agreeing with prastha) is the plain reading.

hindi: सब अतिसारों में यह बल के अनुसार पीना चाहिए।
english: In all atisāras (diarrhoeas), this is to be drunk according to strength.
notes: 'this' refers to the ghee of 154-156. 'yathābalam' = according to the strength (of the patient is the natural sense, but the text does not say whose).

words.gloss: samaṅgā (disputed; Mimosa pudica is often given)

hindi: कच्छुरा, धातकी यानी धाय, बिल्व यानी बेल, समंगा यानी सम्भवतः लाजवन्ती और रक्तमूली से,
english: With kacchurā, dhātakī (woodfordia), bilva (wood-apple), samaṅgā (probably touch-me-not; disputed) and raktamūlin,
notes: GROUPING: 158 and 159 form one statement (yavāgū, 159). Identifications: kacchurā disputed (no botanical name given); dhātakī standard; bilva standard; samaṅgā disputed (Mimosa pudica often given); raktamūlin unidentified (read as 'red-rooted'). The last member is an instrumental plural, the others are compound members.

words.gloss: aśvattha (sacred fig, Ficus religiosa; standard); tips, shoots

hindi: और मसूर और पीपल की कोंपलों से, जल में उबालने पर, यवागू यानी लपसी हो।
english: And with masūra (lentil) and aśvattha (sacred fig) tips, boiled in water, there should be a yavāgū (gruel).
notes: Completes 158. 'masūraśvatthaśṛṅgaiḥ' is read as masūra + aśvattha-śṛṅga (shoots of the aśvattha); a reading of three separate items (masūra, aśvattha, śṛṅga) is also possible. Which of the things listed in 158-159 are boiled is not stated precisely.

words.gloss: young; udumbara (cluster fig); kaṭvaṅga (disputed; Oroxylum indicum often given); samaṅgā (see 158); plakṣa (probably Ficus virens, pilkhan; probable); sprouts

hindi: कोमल गूलर, कट्वंग यानी सम्भवतः सोनापाठा, समंगा और प्लक्ष यानी पाकड़ की कोंपलों से,
english: With the sprouts (pallava) of young udumbara, kaṭvaṅga (probably Oroxylum indicum; disputed), samaṅgā and plakṣa (probably a fig, pilkhan),
notes: GROUPING: 160 and 161 form one statement (predicate 'tathā bhavet' in 161, i.e. likewise a yavāgū). Whether 'bāla' (young) governs only udumbara or all members is not clear; the plain reading is the first. Identifications: kaṭvaṅga disputed (Oroxylum indicum often given; some give Ailanthus); plakṣa probable (Ficus virens).

words.gloss: masūra (lentil); dhātakī (woodfordia); flowers; balā (country mallow, Sida cordifolia; standard)

hindi: और मसूर, धातकी के फूल और बला यानी खरैटी से भी उसी प्रकार हो।
english: And with masūra, dhātakī flowers and balā (country mallow), it should be likewise.
notes: Completes 160; 'it' is the yavāgū of 159 (not named in this unit). The compound 'masūradhātakīpuṣpabalābhiḥ' is read as masūra + dhātakī-puṣpa + balā; 'dhātakī flowers' is the plain reading, with 'masūra' a separate member.

hindi: बस्ति के विभ्रम से अनेक प्रकार की व्यापदें उत्पन्न होती हैं।
english: Mishaps (vyāpad) of various kinds arise from an error (vibhrama) in the basti.
notes: 'vibhrama' = error, deviation, confusion; kept as 'error'. 'nānāprakārā jāyante' is regular sandhi (āḥ before j). Here the chapter turns back to the mishaps of basti named in its title.

hindi: मार्ग के अनुसार, अवस्था के अनुसार, उनका साधन करे।
english: According to the path, according to the condition, one should carry out the treatment (sādhana) of those.
notes: 'yathāpatham' is obscure: 'path' could mean the course or route of the mishap; a misreading for 'yathāpathyam' (as is suitable) is conceivable but not applied. 'sādhana' = accomplishing, treating; kept with a gloss.

hindi: इस प्रकार बस्तिव्यापत्सिद्धि नामक छठा अध्याय।
english: Thus the sixth chapter, named Bastivyāpatsiddhi.
notes: Chapter colophon (Kalpasthāna chapter 6). The closing 'iti' is the usual end-mark. Title as in unit 1: basti-vyāpat-siddhi, 'accomplishment (success) concerning the mishaps of basti'.
